setup_summary.text: NVIDIA reports fiscal Q3 2027 on 2026-11-17 after the close. Consensus is revenue of $111.36B and EPS of $2.53. That is about 95% year-over-year revenue growth, down from 106% in Q2. The options market implies a ±8.7% move, against a ±4.0% average closing move over the last 8 reports. The record is 4 beats and 0 misses, with a +3.4% average surprise.

Q2 FY27 (reported 8/26): revenue $96.22B (+106% y/y, +18% q/q), GAAP gross margin 75.0%, operating income $63.7B (66.2% margin), diluted EPS $2.46 (+128% y/y). Data Center was $89.0B, with hyperscale $48.7B (+13% q/q) and AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise (ACIE) $40.3B (+25% q/q, +138% y/y).

Q3 guide is revenue of $108B ±2% (about $105.8B–$110.2B), GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin of 74% ±50bp, GAAP opex of about $9.2B and non-GAAP opex of about $9.0B. Vera Rubin is about 20% of Q3 Data Center revenue. The outlook excludes China data center compute revenue. Management called it supply-constrained. Q3 growth is led by ACIE, with hyperscale reaccelerating in Q4.

Consensus revenue of $111.36B sits about 3.1% above the guide midpoint and about 1% above the top of the guided range. It implies about +15.7% sequential growth from $96.2B. The last two quarters grew about +19.8% (Q1: $81.6B on a derived Q4 FY26 of $68.1B) and +18% (Q2).

Management gave a first-ever full-year view: FY28 revenue growth of about 70%, supply-constrained, against demand growth the CEO described as about 100% or 'much higher'. Supply is expected to stay a bottleneck at least through the end of FY28.

The margin reset is the other main driver of the print. Management guided Q3 to 74%, Q4 to bottom at 71–72%, and FY28 to 72–73% after executed price increases in Q1. It blamed memory prices that exceeded its prior expectations and are 'headed even higher into next year'. Q2 gross margin was 75.0%.

Balance-sheet and financing exposure has grown quickly. Supply commitments rose from $119B to $279B. Guarantees total $108.5B, including $105B for SB Energy/OpenAI. AI-cloud commitments are $36B and equity investments are $99B, with $25B more committed. Debt is $33.4B after a $25B June issuance. Receivables are $63.1B and inventory is $31.6B.
Sentiment is supportive. The consensus price target is $339.17, 65.7% above the $204.64 price. Needham (10/22) and Cantor (10/1) both maintained positive ratings.

view.text: Guide is 74% ±50bp for Q3, with margins guided to bottom at 71–72% in Q4. Q2 gross margin was roughly flat sequentially because Blackwell remains the vast majority of revenue, and Rubin is about 20% of Data Center revenue in Q3. Inventory and purchase-obligation provisions net cost about 0.8 points of margin in Q2. One point of margin on the $108B revenue guide is about $1.08B of gross profit, or roughly $0.04 of EPS at the Q2 16.5% tax rate and 24.3B diluted shares. The Q4 margin guide matters more than the Q3 number.

view.text: At the guide midpoint ($108B, 74% gross margin, $9.0B non-GAAP opex, 16% tax, about 24.2B shares) with no equity gains, EPS is about $2.46. On GAAP opex of $9.2B it is about $2.43. Reaching $2.53 needs revenue of about $111B or more, so the whole gap to consensus is a revenue beat and does not need equity gains. The ±2% revenue band is about ±$0.055 of EPS. This is my estimate.

since_filing.text: Hugging Face deal (8-K, 9/3). NVIDIA agreed to buy Hugging Face for about $11.9B plus up to about $1.0B of equity retention, with closing expected in 1H 2027 subject to regulatory approvals. NVIDIA committed to keep the platform open. Press reports put the total at $12.9–13B, which is consistent with the sum. The 8-K adds a risk factor on government restrictions on models, including those originating in China.

Regulatory scrutiny is new. On 10/28 Reuters, via Bloomberg, reported that the US Justice Department is making inquiries about the Hugging Face deal and looking at NVIDIA's sales practices. The question is whether the deal could give NVIDIA control of a key distribution hub. This is a news report and not a company disclosure.

Hyperscaler capex is mixed but very large. Amazon's Q3 capex was $77.3B against $58.7B expected. Microsoft cut its 2026 capex forecast to $170B from $175B and Alphabet held $195–205B, both below estimates. Meta guided $135–145B. Business Insider puts the aggregate for Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and SpaceX at $803–828B for 2026, against management's 'nearly $800B' for the top five.

Neocloud capacity is a soft spot for the ACIE-led Q3 guide. Microsoft's CFO said third-party GPU providers had delays pushing some capacity into 1H27, and expects capex to accelerate then on component costs and delayed deliveries. Neocloud shares fell, lenders are reported to be pulling back, and NVIDIA-backed Firmus withdrew its IPO. Hyperscaler capex is still expected to top $1T next year.

Memory supplier evidence supports NVIDIA's cost argument. SK Hynix reported record Q3 results on 10/27–29, with revenue +327.9% and operating profit +632.1% y/y, beating estimates. Reuters puts operating profit at 83 trillion won. Its shareholder-return figure differs by source: more than $25B at CNBC and $75B at Reuters. TrendForce-sourced reporting (10/24) has Q4 DRAM contract prices rising about 20% q/q, a slower pace. Micron's FY26 10-K shows DRAM average selling prices up in the low 40s percent and gross margin of 81%.

Frontier-lab funding is active. Reuters (10/19–20) reports OpenAI seeking about $30B at a valuation above $1.4T ahead of an Anthropic IPO. CNBC reports Anthropic is set to go public and that OpenAI has said a 2027 IPO is likely. These counterparties are a large share of NVIDIA's ecosystem exposure, so their funding and listings matter for the financing debate.

Intel's Q3 (10-Q filed 10/30) shows DCAI revenue of $7.3B against $4.1B a year earlier, at a 42% operating margin. AMD's Data Center revenue was $6.7B (+107%) in the June quarter, with a 54% gross margin. Both remain a fraction of NVIDIA's $89.0B Data Center revenue.

key_debates.question: Is consensus above the guide top end beatable, or is the quarter supply-capped?

bull.text: Consensus of $111.36B needs +15.7% sequential growth, below the roughly +18–20% of the last two quarters. Management says demand far exceeds supply, Rubin production shipments have started, and supply commitments rose to $279B to support the ramp.

bear.text: Consensus is already about 1% above the top of the guide. Management calls the outlook supply-constrained, expects hyperscale to reaccelerate only in Q4, and relies on ACIE for Q3 growth. Microsoft flagged delays at third-party GPU providers and neocloud financing is tightening.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The reported Q3 revenue against $110.2B, the ACIE and hyperscale split, the Rubin share (guided about 20%) and the Q4 revenue guide.

key_debates.question: How deep and how credible is the gross-margin reset?

bull.text: The Q4 trough of 71–72% is roughly the FY26 average of 71.1%, and FY28 is guided to 72–73% after price increases in Q1. Management says tight memory is a symptom of the same demand surge driving its growth, and it has long relationships with all three memory suppliers.

bear.text: Memory pricing has exceeded management's expectations and is 'headed even higher'. Q4 DRAM contract prices are expected to rise about 20% q/q, Micron's gross margin is 81%, and SK Hynix posted record profit. That shows memory suppliers capturing the cost. The recovery depends on price increases that have not yet taken effect.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 gross margin against 74% ±50bp, whether the Q4 guide sits inside or below 71–72%, and any evidence price increases are being accepted for Q1.

key_debates.question: Is the ecosystem financing a demand multiplier or a circularity and counterparty risk?

bull.text: Management says the roughly $50B invested in frontier labs is a small fraction of expected free cash flow, that the compute is fungible and redeployable, and that the compute shipped will be consumed by investment-grade customers or those backed by one. It also describes the $500B third-party financing platforms as independently underwritten.

bear.text: Guarantees total $108.5B, AI-cloud commitments are $36B, supply commitments are $279B, and receivables are $63.1B with five customers each holding at least 10%. The 10-Q adds a new risk factor on counterparty and recovery risk, and management expects AI labs it supports with its balance sheet to be about a quarter of next year's business.

key_debates.what_settles_it: DSO, receivables and free cash flow conversion in Q3, any new guarantees or commitments, whether the $500B platforms become definitive, and the OpenAI and Anthropic funding and listing outcomes.

key_debates.question: Does custom silicon cap NVIDIA's share and pricing?

bull.text: Management says NVIDIA runs every frontier model, closed and open, and that Vera Rubin raises its revenue per gigawatt to about $40B from about $25B with Blackwell. NVIDIA's Data Center revenue of $89.0B is about 4.3x Broadcom's entire semiconductor segment of $20.8B.

bear.text: Broadcom's semiconductor segment grew 127% y/y, faster than NVIDIA's Data Center at 117%, led by custom AI accelerators. A single distributor was 50% of Broadcom's revenue. Its AI XPV platform is financing more than 20 gigawatts for frontier labs through 2028. Frontier labs are NVIDIA's own financing recipients and are also building custom chips.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Rubin ramp and its share of Data Center revenue, the FY28 hyperscale re-acceleration, and whether the Q1 price increases hold against custom-silicon pricing.

scenarios.name: bear

Receivables and DSO rise further and free cash flow conversion stays weak. New guarantees and commitments, or a DOJ escalation on Hugging Face, add to the circular-financing worry.

triggers: DSO above 60 days and free cash flow conversion below H1's roughly 59%
Further growth in guarantees or equity commitments
Neocloud financing stress or customer delay disclosures

claim.text: Commitments, guarantees and counterparty risk: $108.5B of guarantees (including $105B for SB Energy/OpenAI, effective from FY2029), $36B of AI-cloud commitments and $25B of equity commitments. The 10-Q added a new risk factor saying customers may fail to fulfil obligations, that NVIDIA may be unable to reduce its own commitments if demand differs, and that recovery from OpenAI may not be prompt or full.

Supply and inventory exposure: supply commitments rose from $119B to $279B in a quarter and inventory was $31.6B. If demand is smaller than planned, the 10-Q says NVIDIA may be unable to reduce commitments, and Q2 provisions already cost about 0.8 points of gross margin.

Memory-cost and gross-margin risk: management guided gross margin down to a 71–72% trough in Q4 and says memory costs are rising beyond its expectations. The recovery depends on price increases in Q1 that are not yet in the numbers.

Working-capital quality: DSO rose to 60 days on extended terms of up to one year for investment-grade customers. Receivables rose $24.6B in H1. Five direct customers held about 70% of receivables, and one customer was 16% of Q2 revenue. H1 free cash flow converted only about 59% of net income.

Equity-portfolio volatility in GAAP results: H1 equity gains were $23.7B and marketable equity was $42.8B, most of it under lock-up. The 10-Q warns that additional investments could materially affect carrying value. GAAP EPS can diverge sharply from operating results in either direction.

Regulatory and deal risk: the DOJ is reported to be making inquiries about the Hugging Face acquisition and NVIDIA's sales practices. The 10-Q also lists broad competition-regulator requests in the EU, US, UK, China and South Korea, and China's preliminary September 2025 finding on the Mellanox approval.

China and export policy: NVIDIA says it is effectively foreclosed from China data center compute. H200 shipments carry a 25% tariff it cannot pass on and were under 1% of Data Center revenue. The GAIN AI Act and RASA remain open risks. China is excluded from guidance, so policy change is optionality rather than a base-case driver.

Customer and neocloud financing risk: the ACIE segment drives Q3 growth and depends on neoclouds that need outside capital. Microsoft cited delays at third-party GPU providers, lenders are reported to be pulling back and Firmus withdrew its IPO. A tight credit market could slow ACIE shipments.

questions_for_management.question: Q3 revenue is guided to $108B but consensus is $111.4B. How much of the supply you secure is available in Q3 versus Q4, and what limits upside this quarter: wafers, HBM, packaging or rack integration?

why.text: Management calls the outlook supply-constrained and consensus sits above the top of the range.

questions_for_management.question: Give a bridge for the gross-margin decline from 75% to the Q4 trough of 71–72%: memory cost, Rubin mix, Groq LPX ramp and inventory provisions. How much of the Q1 FY28 price increase is already contracted?

why.text: Management gave no split of the decline and the recovery to 72–73% depends on price increases that take effect in Q1.

questions_for_management.question: DSO rose to 60 days on extended terms for investment-grade customers. What is the expected peak DSO, how long are the longest terms, and what credit insurance or collateral covers them?

why.text: Receivables rose $24.6B in H1, five customers hold about 70% of the balance, and terms can run up to one year.

questions_for_management.question: What is the total cash and credit exposure across guarantees, AI-cloud take-or-pay commitments, equity commitments and residual-value support in FY28, and when do the $500B financing platforms become definitive?

why.text: Guarantees total $108.5B and AI-cloud commitments $36B, and the platforms are still MOUs. Management also expects labs backed by its balance sheet to be about a quarter of next year's business.

questions_for_management.question: Microsoft said third-party GPU providers had delays. Are you seeing neocloud or ACIE customers delaying deployments or struggling to finance them, and how is that reflected in the Q3 guide?

why.text: The Q3 guide relies on ACIE for sequential growth, and Microsoft cited delays at third-party GPU providers that push capacity into 1H27.

data_gaps: The consensus basis for the $2.53 EPS (GAAP or non-GAAP) is not confirmed. If it is GAAP, it would need equity gains or a larger revenue beat. The 8/26 non-GAAP EPS of $2.22 reported by Investing.com is outside the 14-day window and background only.

Prior-quarter guide-versus-actual history (Q4 FY26 guide $65B, Q1 FY27 $78B, Q2 FY27 $91B, each beaten by about 4.6–5.7% at the midpoint) comes from older news outside the 14-day window and is not cited as evidence. Extrapolating that cadence to $108B gives about $113B. That is background arithmetic, not a sourced forecast.
No sell-side estimates for Q4 FY27 or FY28 gross margin or revenue were found, and no high/low range for Q3 revenue estimates. Whisper EPS is not yet looked up (the print is 17 days out).
No post-8/26 results or channel checks from TSMC, Samsung or Micron's latest quarter were retrieved. HBM pricing guidance in the SK Hynix coverage was truncated.

The Bloomberg report (8/22) that NVIDIA told large customers of server price increases above 15% on systems shipping early next year is outside the 14-day window, so it is not cited. No newer source confirms executed increases.

No Rubin delay, yield, HBM or rack-level problem was found in the sources, but absence of reports is not proof there are none. The earlier SemiAnalysis note on HBM4 bandwidth is dated February and not cited.
The Jefferies call that Rubin exceeds 40% of revenue by fiscal year-end, and the 8/27 premarket move, could not be verified against in-window sources and are not used.

China status: no news from the last 14 days on H200 licensing, export rules, GAIN AI/RASA or the SAMR probe. Whether the 75,000-per-customer H200 cap was adopted and whether SAMR closed its probe are unestablished. The 10-Q still carries the SAMR finding as a live risk.
Quarterly free cash flow split (Q1 $48.6B, Q2 $21.3B) comes from an 8/28 third-party article outside the window. Only the H1 total of about $70B is derived from filings.

Broadcom does not break out AI revenue in the retrieved 10-Q passages, so the 4.3x NVIDIA-to-Broadcom ratio is a floor using its whole semiconductor segment. No AMD Q3 report date or MI450 revenue timing was found, and no Google TPU volumes.

SK Hynix's shareholder-return figure conflicts across sources ($25B+ at CNBC versus $75B at Reuters). The Amazon press release (N.70) carries a May date stamp despite describing Q3 results, so its AWS growth figure is not used.
Share count for Q3 EPS (about 24.2B diluted) and the tax and interest assumptions in my EPS bridge are my own and ignore any change in other income.

A claim was removed because its sources don't support it: 'Management said it will return excess free cash flow net of strategic uses. H1 free cash flow was $69.99B against net income of $118.01B, about 59% conversion. Equity investment commitments were $25B at July 26, up from $11.4B investment commitments at year-end.' (The passages give $25B of equity investment commitments at July 26, 2026, but nothing for year-end showing $11.4B of investment commitments, so the 'up from' comparison has no source (the K.255 passage covers only supply commitments and debt).).
